geo.label: on hold / cuts back in play
parts: Macro Stance

January payrolls rose by 130,000 [[n6773]] and headline CPI cooled to 2.4%, less than expected [[n7371]], but core CPI picked up on firmer services costs [[n6783]]. That lets the Fed wait without closing the door: traders boosted bets to 50% for three cuts this year [[n7359]]. Mixed — the macro is fine; the equity tape is trading AI-disruption fear.
Rates & Curve

The 2Y closed at 3.40% and the 10Y at 4.04%, a 10Y−2Y spread of +64 bps; over 20 observations the 2Y fell 16 bps and the 10Y 13 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-13). The curve is moderately steep, approaching the long-run average, after a bull steepening (both down, 2Y down more). Equities missed the relief: the S&P 500 closed at 6,836.17, down 1.56% over 20 sessions, with the VIX at 20.60 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).
New / Most Important

Senator Tillis will not support confirming the Fed-chair nominee until the DOJ investigation of Powell is done [[n7532]] — a slower handover keeps the current, patient committee in charge for longer. The limited government shutdown is likely to linger at least 10 days as Congress takes a break [[n7506]], adding headline risk but little GDP drag.
Playbook ✓

Own the 5Y at 3.61% as the cleanest expression of the cut repricing (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-13), and stay underweight the Nasdaq 100 (QQQ down 3.19% over 20 sessions) against industrials (XLI up 5.06%) until Nvidia reports (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Change the call if a hot core print lifts the 2Y back above 3.56%, its level 20 observations ago (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-13).

geo.label: ECB on hold / inflows rotate in
parts: Macro Stance

Europe is the relative winner of the AI scare. Euro-area GDP rose 0.3% in the latest quarterly estimate [[n2636]], inflation fell to 1.7% in January [[n2415]], and the ECB is extending its longest rate pause since the negative-rate era [[n2560]] — below-target inflation gives Frankfurt an easing option the Fed lacks.
Activity & Inflation

The STOXX 600 closed at 617.70, up 0.54% over 20 sessions against a 1.56% fall in the S&P 500, while EUR/USD at 1.1868 is up 2.23%, itself a disinflation channel (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Money is following: Europe and Asia led equity fund inflows as the US recorded a weekly outflow [[n2657]].
New / Most Important

The AI scare has reached European software: Dassault Systèmes plunged 18%, on track for its worst day ever [[n2104]]. Europe outperforms because it is short software and long banks, energy and industrials — the FTSE 100's 2.06% 20-session gain against the DAX's 1.51% loss shows the mix (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).
Playbook ✓

Overweight European banks and domestic cyclicals against US growth; prefer the FTSE 100's value mix to the DAX's export and software tilt, funded from software and China-exposed luxury. Change the view if euro-area inflation turns back up or the fund-flow rotation reverses toward the US for several weeks.

geo.label: moderately loose / managed bull
parts: Macro Stance

China heads into the Lunar New Year with deflation easing at the margin but private demand still soft. The policy mix is supportive — moderately loose money, a large grid programme and a trade truce — yet households are not borrowing and housing is still falling. We stay Mixed: policy is putting a floor under activity and markets, but there is no self-sustaining recovery to buy yet.
PMIs & Activity

The latest official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in January [[n0530]], back in contraction territory. Autos are the visible weak spot: January car sales fell at the fastest pace in nearly two years [[n0713]], the clearest sign that discount-driven demand is fading. The February PMIs need to show the official index back above 50 before we treat the January dip as noise; until then, read activity as flat at best.
Credit Impulse

January new loans jumped but missed forecasts as weak demand persists [[n0864]]. The PBOC pledged to keep policy moderately loose [[n0736]], but credit supply is not the constraint — household and private-sector demand is. Until household lending turns, the impulse flows into financial assets rather than capex, which is why onshore equities have held up better than the activity data.
Property

New home prices extended their decline in January [[n6741]], and support is becoming more direct: Shenzhen is drafting an $11.6 billion rescue package for China Vanke [[n0718]]. A state-led backstop for a systemically important developer cuts tail risk for banks and bondholders, but it does not create buyers. Treat a slower pace of decline as the best case for 2026, not a floor, and keep developers out of the portfolio.
Fiscal, Policy & Trade

The clearest capex line is the plan to invest 5 trillion yuan in the power grid over five years [[n0685]] — a multi-year order book for transformers, cables and switchgear that does not depend on housing. On trade, Reuters reported Trump paused China tech bans ahead of a Xi summit [[n0821]], extending the trade truce. The near-term risk is that the summit slips and the bans return.
Markets & Flows

The Hang Seng closed at 26,567.12, down 1.72% in the prior session and 1.03% over 20 sessions; the Shanghai Composite ended at 4,082.07, off 0.48% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). In New York, ASHR held at 33.68 (down 0.82% over 20 sessions) while KWEB fell to 32.79 (down 9.87%) and FXI to 38.33 (down 4.17%); USD/CNY slipped 0.95% to 6.9001 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Onshore A-shares and the currency are being managed for stability, while the offshore internet complex is where the selling concentrates.
New / Most Important

The biggest single-company signal is Meituan's warning of a $3.5 billion loss from the food-delivery price war [[n0873]]. It explains KWEB's 9.87% 20-session drop better than any macro print: the platform names are spending their profits to defend share (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Until a truce among the delivery platforms appears, internet is a margin story, not a growth story.
Playbook ✓

Prefer onshore A-shares (ASHR) and grid-equipment suppliers tied to the 5 trillion yuan programme over platform internet (KWEB). Keep a long-CNY bias against the dollar while USD/CNY trends lower. Upgrade to Bullish on a credit print that beats forecasts with stronger household lending; downgrade if new-home price declines re-accelerate or the tech-ban pause is reversed. ⚠ Divergence: factory-gate deflation eased more than forecast in January [[n6619]], which says reflation may arrive faster than the credit data imply.

The Nikkei 225 closed at 56,941.97, up 5.23% over 20 sessions despite a 1.21% drop in the prior session; USD/JPY fell to 152.82, down 3.64% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Own the yen against the dollar and Japanese banks over exporters, whose margins a stronger yen compresses. Reverse if the Ueda meeting signals pressure to delay hikes, or if USD/JPY reclaims 158.6, its level 20 sessions ago (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

geo.label: hiking / strong AUD
parts: Macro Stance

The RBA has turned from easing to tightening: it raised the cash rate to 3.85% after three cuts [[n0087]], and Bullock said it will raise again if inflation becomes entrenched [[n0215]]. Australia is out of sync with the global easing cycle, which is why the Aussie has outrun the euro, sterling and the yen against the dollar over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

AUD/USD closed at 0.7087, up 5.71% over 20 sessions and 2.47% over five, while the ASX 200 stood at 8,917.60, up 0.63% over 20 sessions after a 1.39% fall in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Playbook ✓

Stay long AUD against the dollar and own the major banks with deposit franchises, which earn more on a higher cash rate; underweight rate-sensitive retailers and housing-linked names. Change the call if monthly CPI rolls over decisively, or if reporting-season guidance shows the strong currency crushing exporter earnings.

Trading desks gain from volatility and lower yields support loan demand, but the group is priced on AI and private-credit exposure, so beats will not be rewarded until that fear fades.

The real risk sits in credit, not deposits: Bloomberg reports private credit's software bet is even bigger than it appears [[n5533]]. If software borrowers are the AI losers, their lenders are second-order losers — avoid alternative managers and BDCs before the big banks.

Energy leads the 20-session sector table: XLE closed at 54.35, up 14.16% over 20 sessions, with Exxon up 14.96% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). OPEC+ leans toward resuming output increases from April [[n5525]], so the bull case rests on Iran risk rather than supply. Own XLE as a geopolitical hedge, not as a call on oil fundamentals, and trim into any spike.

XLI closed at 174.17, up 5.06% over 20 sessions, and Caterpillar is up 19.63% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). The macro anchor is the January ISM manufacturing PMI at 52.6% [[n6342]] — the factory cycle is turning just as AI and grid capex accelerate.

Grid and power-equipment suppliers: China alone plans 5 trillion yuan of grid investment over five years [[n0685]], on top of US utility capex plans. Caterpillar's power-generation business gives it the same exposure, and transformer and switchgear makers sit in the same slipstream.

The consumer is K-shaped: US firms confront a widening gulf as the wealthy spend and budget shoppers struggle [[n6668]]. That favours luxury travel and big-box value, and squeezes everything in between — the sector average hides two opposite trades.

Staples are the AI-scare refuge: XLP closed at 89.51, up 8.67% over 20 sessions, with Walmart up 12.32% and Costco 6.45% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Walmart's results headline the week ahead [[n0321]], so the group's leadership faces a hard test.

UnitedHealth rose 3.10% in the prior session but sits 13.50% lower over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). Managed care now carries low expectations, which is the precondition for upside surprises once medical-cost trends stabilise.

XLU closed at 46.50, up 2.76% in the prior session, 7.27% over five and 6.63% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13): utilities are bid both as bond proxies and as AI infrastructure. Duke claims the largest spending plan of any regulated US utility at $103B [[n2254]].

Rate-base growth is the reported story — capex plans keep rising, and the market is paying for them. NextEra closed at 93.80, up 14.13% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

Memory and equipment carry the strongest price momentum; AMD, at 207.32 and down 9.04% over 20 sessions, and Intel, down 7.51% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), are the laggards where expectations are now low.

Nvidia is the laggard inside a winning sector, down 2.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13) and stalled despite $600 billion of AI capex [[n5503]]. The market is paying the bottlenecks (memory, tools), not the platform — until Nvidia's results reset that.

earnings_pattern.title: Physical AI gets paid; seat-based software and intermediaries get fined
parts: Rewarded

Results that show AI as demand rather than threat: Applied Materials jumped [[n2198]] and Siemens rose on a lifted outlook [[n2249]]. Self-help with credible guidance also paid — Airbnb rose on a revenue beat and rosy guidance [[n2181]].
Punished

Beats did not protect anyone whose outlook is clouded by AI or tariffs: Cisco fell 7% despite topping estimates [[n2099]], Dassault Systèmes plunged 18% [[n2104]] and Pinterest sank nearly 17% [[n2318]]. Payout cuts were punished even in the market's strongest sector — BP fell 7% after suspending its buyback [[n2009]].
Pattern

The market pays for capacity and pricing power (memory, semicap, automation, grid) and fines revenue earned per seat, per transaction or per ad click. Guidance outranks the quarter, and a capital-return cut outranks both. Over 20 sessions the gap is stark: Micron up 22.29% and Caterpillar 19.63%, against Microsoft down 12.12% and Amazon 16.54% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).
Attention into EPS

Walmart and fresh economic data lead the week ahead [[n0321]]; Hims & Hers reports on February 23 [[n1508]]; and Nvidia's Feb. 25 date has Wall Street giving a nearly unanimous answer on buying beforehand [[n7408]]. In Australia, 80 companies prepare to report [[n0303]] — the first large sample of how a higher cash rate and a strong AUD hit guidance.
Playbook

Buy beats with raised guides in physical-AI, grid and memory; fade beats with flat guides in seat-based software, payments and ad platforms until the AI-proof baskets outperform. Use Walmart [[n0321]] as the test of the defensive rotation: a beat that still sells off means staples are exhausted and the next leg is a rotation back toward beaten-down growth.

underowned.title: US Gulf refiners — the Venezuela heavy-crude unlock
parts: Attention Gap

Venezuela is read as a crude-supply headline, yet the cleaner equity lever is refining: the US eased sanctions to give majors broad scope to operate [[n3291]], which puts more heavy crude within reach of Gulf Coast plants built to process it. Attention has gone to the majors — XLE is up 14.16% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13) — not to the refiners that capture the discount.
Exposure & Risk

Express through Valero and other complex Gulf Coast refiners or a refining ETF (CRAK) rather than more XLE. Risk: an Iran disruption would lift crude faster than product margins, and an OPEC+ output restart from April [[n5525]] would narrow the heavy-crude discount refiners are counting on.

crypto.title: Washed-out shorts meet a down-trend that has not turned
parts: Market Context

Positioning is washed out, the trend is not. Prefer bitcoin over ether until ETH stops underperforming, and treat MSTR and COIN as short-dated options on a squeeze, not as core holdings.

flows.title: Bull steepener, softer dollar, tight credit with an AI-debt tail
parts: Rates & Dollar

DXY closed at 96.88, down 2.46% over 20 sessions, while TLT rose 2.49% over five sessions to 89.72 and IEF 1.19% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13). The curve did the work: the 10Y fell 18 bps over five observations to 4.04%, and the 2s10s sits at +64 bps in a bull steepening (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-13). A falling dollar alongside falling yields is a growth-scare-lite signal, not a funding stress.
Credit Check

HYG closed at 80.85 (down 0.23% over 20 sessions) and LQD at 111.59 (up 0.63%) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13): spreads are holding while equity volatility rises. Supply is the story — Alphabet placed almost $32 billion of bonds [[n2792]], and investment grade is absorbing AI capex without strain. If stress comes, it will show first in high-yield software borrowers, not in the hyperscalers' paper.
Portfolio Implication

Rotate from US large-cap growth into duration and non-US equities, following the flow: Europe and Asia led equity fund inflows as the US recorded a weekly outflow [[n2657]]. Hold investment grade at benchmark, underweight high-yield software borrowers and BDCs. Revisit if HYG extends its 20-session decline while TLT stops rallying — that combination would mark a credit event rather than an equity rotation.

anticipatory.title: US-Iran: weeks-long operations or a nuclear compromise
parts: What Is Priced

Washington is escalating — the US military is preparing for potentially weeks-long Iran operations [[n3368]] — while Iran says it is ready to discuss compromises to reach a nuclear deal [[n3369]], and, according to a source, separate Iran and Ukraine talks are set for Tuesday in Geneva [[n3340]]. Oil prices little of this: Brent sits at 67.75, up 6.26% over 20 sessions, and the VIX at 20.60 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).
Conditional Expression

If strikes begin: Brent call spreads, XLE and tanker owners, long gold (already up 9.14% over 20 sessions at 5,046.30) and short airlines (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13); the OPEC+ April restart [[n5525]] caps the move only if Gulf flows are untouched. If Geneva yields a framework: fade the energy premium — XLE's 14.16% 20-session gain is the unwind candidate — and add European cyclicals and EM oil importers (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).
Risk

Both outcomes are headline-driven and can reverse within a session; a limited operation could still disrupt shipping, and a deal could stall after an initial relief rally. Keep both legs in options rather than cash positions, and size for gap risk on Asian opens.

anticipatory.title: Ukraine talks in Geneva: peace dividend versus defence bid
parts: What Is Priced

Ukraine-Russia talks are set for Tuesday in Geneva alongside the Iran track [[n3340]]. Polish and European assets already price a constructive path: EPOL is up 4.2% over 20 sessions, USD/PLN down 2.12% and the STOXX 600 up 0.54% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), while gas at 3.24 on Henry Hub shows no energy-stress premium in the US.
Conditional Expression

Progress: long European cyclicals and autos (SXAP), PLN and Polish banks, and short European gas exposure; trim defence winners. Breakdown: defence and the SAFE-funded Polish supply chain re-rate higher and PLN gives back gains — hedge with EUR/PLN calls and own European defence primes.
Risk

Europe's own security exposure stays unresolved whatever is agreed in Geneva, so a 'peace' framework could still support European defence budgets, and any deal could stall in EU capitals after an initial relief rally. Size the cyclical leg modestly until terms are public.

catalysts.title: $WMT — the print that tests the staples rotation
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Walmart's results lead the week ahead [[n0321]]. The K-shaped consumer favours the scale grocer: the wealthy keep spending while budget shoppers struggle [[n6668]], so Walmart gains trips at both ends, and the AI scare keeps money hunting for defensive growth.
Price Hurdle & Risk

WMT closed at 133.89, up 12.32% over 20 sessions and 2.07% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13), so the bar is high. Express with a call spread rather than stock; exit if the shares fall on a beat, which would signal the staples rotation is spent.

catalysts.title: $NVDA — the cheapest AI exposure into its Feb. 25 date
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

The Motley Fool frames Feb. 25 as the decision point, saying Wall Street is providing a nearly unanimous answer on buying Nvidia beforehand [[n7408]]. The thesis: the stock has stalled despite $600 billion of AI capex [[n5503]], so expectations sit below the demand signal, and a guide that confirms hyperscaler spending can re-rate the platform the market has been ignoring in favour of memory and tools.
Price Hurdle & Risk

NVDA closed at 182.81, down 2.21% in the prior session and 2.27% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13); a reclaim of 187.05, its level 20 sessions ago, confirms the call. Risks: margin pressure from memory costs and any sign that customers are stretching capex with debt rather than cash flow.

catalysts.title: $HIMS — crowded short into results
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Hims & Hers reports on February 23 [[n1508]], with hedge funds betting big against it before a Wegovy showdown [[n2993]]. The cash-pay obesity niche looks exposed: after its bleak 2026 forecast [[n1665]], Novo has every incentive to fight for cash-pay patients, and branded price competition erodes the compounding model's discount.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Use defined-risk put spreads into the print rather than an outright short. The danger is the crowding itself: a clean beat or a partnership headline could squeeze shorts violently, so cut the position on any upside guidance revision.

retail.title: Micron & Sandisk / MU, SNDK — the memory-squeeze momentum trade
parts: Observed Attention

Yahoo Finance asks whether SanDisk, up 163% in 2026, can be the market's top performer in back-to-back years [[n4340]]. MU closed at 411.66, up 22.29% over 20 sessions and 4.3% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).
Motivation & Bias

Extrapolation of a price spike — rampant AI demand for memory is fuelling a chip crisis [[n5774]] — plus the story that memory is the AI winner software is not. Recency bias underrates how fast supply answers when prices spike.
Instrument & Risk

Hold MU over SNDK and trim into extensions; the 0.56% dip in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13) is the kind of pause that turns into a sharp drawdown when the first capacity announcement lands. Use trailing stops rather than averaging up.

retail.title: Silver / SLV, AGQ — the meme-metal whipsaw
parts: Observed Attention

24/7 Wall St. called leveraged AGQ the most hated investment it has seen [[n4257]], and a sudden precious-metals sell-off followed [[n5435]]. SLV closed at 69.72, down 16.32% over 20 sessions despite a 2.94% bounce in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).
Motivation & Bias

A debasement narrative plus bottom-fishing after a crash: retail treats a 15% drawdown as a discount rather than as evidence of a broken trend. Gold's 9.14% 20-session gain (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13) feeds the 'silver must catch up' argument.
Instrument & Risk

Leveraged AGQ's daily-reset decay punishes holders in a choppy range. If you must, hold SLV with a hard stop, or use gold (GLD up 9.28% over 20 sessions) as the lower-volatility substitute (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-13).

retail.title: Robinhood & prediction markets / HOOD — event bets replace coins
parts: Observed Attention
The WSJ says Robinhood got a prediction-market lift despite its cooling crypto business [[n4284]] — a sign retail activity is shifting from coins toward event contracts.
Motivation & Bias
Quick resolution and lottery-style payoffs — the same impulse that drove meme coins, now in a regulated wrapper. The cohort is active, just rotating toward faster bets as crypto prices fall.
Instrument & Risk

HOOD is the listed proxy. Regulatory scrutiny of event contracts and new competitors entering the space could compress take rates, and crypto volumes remain a drag — keep it a trading position, not a core holding.
